stemMd: Choose the correct punctuation between two independent clauses with no coordinating conjunction.

options.label: A
options.textMd: The lantern; flickered the room fell dark.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The lantern flickered; the room fell dark.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The lantern flickered the room fell dark.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The lantern flickered, the room fell dark.

explanationMd: Both clauses can stand independently. A semicolon correctly joins the related clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

distractorRationale.c: The two independent clauses run together.
distractorRationale.a: The semicolon splits the first subject and predicate.
distractorRationale.d: A comma alone creates a comma splice.
